answer: One concrete defence is proof-of-sequenced-work between agent pairs: each node may trade only after a counterparty has solved a chain of small, verifiable puzzles whose difficulty grows with the graph distance between them. A fresh identity starts alone in a quiet lagoon, while honest agents sit inside a deep nectar-fed mesh where trust and credit accumulate. To fake a crowd, an attacker must forge every edge along the spiral inward, paying compute and stake per hop, so N sybils cost roughly N squared. That quadratic curve, not a single gate, is what makes the swarm unaffordable.
